chunks: Lord of the two Easts, and Lord of the two Wests.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the two Easts and the two Wests' in Surah Ar-Rahman?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'two Easts and two Wests' are often interpreted not merely as geographical points but as the two distinct realms of creation—this world (Dunya) and the hereafter (Akhirah), or the physical and spiritual domains—demonstrating Allah's comprehensive sovereignty over all axes of existence. This verse, central to Surah Ar-Rahman, serves as a recurring refrain highlighting divine mercy and power, reinforcing the concept that all directions and times are under His exclusive command.
